sections.id: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP
sections.title: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP

questions.title: Move away from current vendor for integrated CGP and MRD
questions.text: Q19A. Views on integrated CGP + MRD offerings. Some vendors now offer comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) and follow-on tumor-informed MRD monitoring as a single serial workflow, where the up-front profiling overlaps substantially with a standalone CGP test. Thinking about how you would choose among testing options, how much do you agree with the following? I would move away from my current CGP vendor if another vendor offered CGP and subsequent MRD monitoring as a single, integrated serial workflow.
questions.section: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP

questions.title: Use one vendor for profiling and MRD despite CGP preference
questions.text: Q19A. Views on integrated CGP + MRD offerings. I would use a single vendor for both initial profiling and serial MRD monitoring even if its CGP were not my first choice.
questions.section: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP

questions.title: Accept narrower CGP panel integrated with MRD
questions.text: Q19A. Views on integrated CGP + MRD offerings. I would accept a somewhat narrower CGP panel if it were tightly integrated with high-quality MRD monitoring.
questions.section: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP

questions.title: Forego standalone CGP for lower bundled out-of-pocket cost
questions.text: Q19A. Views on integrated CGP + MRD offerings. If bundling CGP and MRD lowered my patients’ overall out-of-pocket cost, I would forgo a standalone CGP from another vendor.
questions.section: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP

questions.title: Continue ordering best-in-class CGP despite bundling
questions.text: Q19A. Views on integrated CGP + MRD offerings. Even if a vendor bundled CGP and MRD, I would still order comprehensive CGP from whichever vendor I consider best-in-class.
questions.section: Section V — MRD: Utilization & Relationship to CGP

questions.title: MRD vendor choice drives CGP choice
questions.text: Q19A. Views on integrated CGP + MRD offerings. In practice, my choice of MRD vendor would drive my choice of CGP, rather than the reverse.

Chrysalis Biomedical Advisors has been retained to better understand the adoption of commercial comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) tests, and the reasons one test is selected over another.
Definition used in this survey
For the purposes of this survery, “Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP)” means a broad multi-gene next-generation sequencing panel (roughly 50+ genes) used for therapy selection in solid tumors — tissue-based or liquid (blood/ctDNA). It excludes single-gene or small hotspot panels, IHC/FISH, hereditary/germline panels, and minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring assays unless a question specifically asks about them.

Definition used in this survey For the purposes of this survery, “Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP)” means a broad multi-gene next-generation sequencing panel (roughly 50+ genes) used for therapy selection in solid tumors — tissue-based or liquid (blood/ctDNA). It excludes single-gene or small hotspot panels, IHC/FISH, hereditary/germline panels, and minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring assays unless a question specifically asks about them.
